description: Small labeled regression corpus for the existing Luminicent JavaScript/TypeScript static analyzer.

cases.rationale: A verified Express handler passes a request query value into concatenated SQL.
Taint should survive two local assignments before reaching the SQL execution sink.
A registered route passes request data through a CommonJS import into an ES module SQL sink.
An unknown implementation named escape must not clear taint.
The SQL statement is static and the request value is supplied separately as a bound parameter.
A static SQL literal has no dynamic input.
A user-defined object method named query is not a database sink; this measures name-based sink false positives.
Both syntactically distinct vulnerable sinks must be matched independently even though they share a line.
The direct SQL pattern remains visible, but dynamic module resolution should be reflected as incomplete project analysis.
Both sinks have explicit expectations while dynamic module loading makes project analysis partial.
Browser URL input is outside the current modeled JavaScript source set; this case is not scored as a clean negative.
Request input reaches a shell-enabled child-process call.
A fixed executable and static argument array contain no dynamic input.
A tainted value in an argument array is measured as argument injection, distinct from shell parsing.
A custom method named exec is not child_process; it traps name-based sink recognition.
A request-derived expression reaches eval in a verified route handler.
The static string is not attacker-controlled, but evaluating code remains a supported dangerous-API indicator rather than a taint-confirmed vulnerability.
A custom object method named eval is not JavaScript code evaluation; this is a false-positive trap.
A timer API receives a code string, a supported dynamic-execution pattern.
Request body data reaches the modeled node-serialize deserialization API.
